newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Britain's Hannay to visit divided Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Hannay to visit divided Cyprus.

text.p: David Hannay, Britain's envoy on the Cyprus issue, will visit the divided island this month for contacts with both the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot sides, the British High Commission said on Friday.
"He will not be bringing a plan with him, but will bring ideas on the main aspects of the Cyprus problem," a British spokesman told Reuters.

Hannay, appointed Britain's special representative on the Cyprus issue earlier this year, will have meetings with Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash during his visit, from October 13 to 18.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkish troops invaded the north in 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military regime ruling Greece.
Some 30,000 troops are stationed in northern Cyprus, declared a Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in 1983 but recognised only by Ankara.
A small army of mediators working under United Nations auspices for more than 20 years to reunite the island as a bicommunal federation have failed to achieve any progress.
